reviews.comment: The lectures were great, the lab equipment was old

The professor presented the course material very well and created an environment that proved that he care about the course. This lab was very hands-on with new skills learned. Must focus and spend enough time though.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The course is very practical. What is in the lecture is what's on the homework and exams. I learned so much about dynamics because of this course. The feedback from Professor Gharib was wonderful.
Easy course if you study for it
very handson course for robotics
It was fun summer course
Excellent teaching style, but too many topics. Exams are similar to lectures and practice problems. The final project was very useful. Lab grading was tough because it is W course.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His lectures don't help much with the midterm, and we didn't get to work with over half the parts discussed in lecture. Things like PID were not gone over in lecture when it's THE ONE thing that should've been gone over with more detail. I already knew half the material so sitting through lecture was boring. Hopefully 375 and onward he's better.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Start on the final project as early as you can. They randomly assign you projects that have to be due THAT day even if you literally just got it. Labs are easy in the beginning but get really hard towards the end. Lab report grades are brutal...good luck even making a 70. There is no homework so lab grades are really all you got to rely on.

This is my 2nd time taking this professor, yet again I am left disappointed and angry. The class material is gone over with minimal detail, provides no homework problems which ends up being detrimental to the student when studying for exams. Final project will genuinely make or break your grade, choose project wisely. Doesn't reply to emails.
Does not proof read his own exams, and then punishes us for his mistakes by taking off our points.

Very test heavy. Make sure you at least attempt lab before class, it will help. Go to office hours to ensure you know what he is looking for. Make sure your project is doable but creative. He takes off for lack creativity and various other things. :)

His teaching in this class is extremely surface level (reading definitions from slides-surface level)but it is expected for you to apply advanced concepts in lab and the final project.This “introductory” class teaches you barely anything in lectures and treats you like an expert.I learned more from the TAs during the labs than the professor himself

Gharib is passionate about this field but too ambitious. Too many topics are barely covered in a couple of lectures. He does not go in enough detail in these lectures to justify the complexity of the labs/final project which are worth 70% of your final grade.

Professor really has a way of making concepts stick, even without posting examples or providing many in class. It's impressive how they manage to explain complex ideas with so few real-world applications. But don't worry — the occasional abstract concept will surely clarify everything for you… eventually!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He cares about his students, but goes about it in ways that only negatively impact them. The grading scheme for exams was not shared before the first exam which greatly hurt everyone. Changed two things on his syllabus without a disclaimer, including taking away formula sheets for the last exam and not posting all of his lecture notes.

Prof is very passionate about the subjects he teaches, but in this class it consists of a many lightly covered topics. The final project is a combination of what is learned in class, but we weren't allowed to use several components we learned about. But the final project is very fun to work on.

He grades harshly and then proceeds to blame the class for not studying enough for his exams. He covers a lot of material but tends to teach fast, occasionally skipping to the end of problems without explaining how he got there. For the final project, he kept supplying us with defective or outdated parts and documentation.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gharib invented this course from scratch to fix many gaps in the degree. Easy lectures, but labs require hard work. Fun project at the end from real-life applications.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very well-organized slides, but you must attend and write after the professor. The professor is very helpful and responds to emails. The lab is great for learning numerical simulation in engineering.

This course lacks depth and practicality, with 5 exams and subjective grading. You must follow the professor's process, as using prior knowledge (e.g., from MMET 370/303 or PHYS 206/207). Different variables not shown in class result in errors. Exams include concepts not taught in class, like linearization, which requires advanced math knowledge.

Dr. Gharib is an excellent teacher for this course. He tries to engage the students in learning the material and holds the students accountable for the effort they put into the work. Additionally, he was always helpful when answering questions regarding coursework.

The most useful hands-on course in robotics. The professor was great and regularly engaged with the class and ensured that due dates and expectations were fair and clearly outlined. Feedback from the lab reports was extremely helpful. The final project was fun and exciting.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: There is so much potential for this course, I had very high hopes and then was unsurprisingly let down. Individual reports due every week, he reads through the lecture slides like he has never seen them before, then expects us to finish a very complicated final project in 3 weeks. It is definitely way too rigorous for a 200 level elective.

Cannot ask him for help because he doesn't know what's going on in labs. Not everyone comes from excessive engineering experience, and the amount of material that is expected to be absorbed and applied in one semester is not healthy and makes the course not enjoyable anymore.

Gharib wants his students to succeed, particularly in the context of the field of robotics, however his class leaves many students feeling frustrated. The tests are graded harshly, with no clear rubric, and based off of how HE solves the problems in lecture, not based off of what would be right. Sometimes the class feels like it lacks direction.

Professor Gharib is a great professor/lecturer and cares how you're doing in his class, if you go to all the lectures, take good notes, and study for the tests you will be fine. The lab gets a bit tedious but is overall pretty easy to succeed in if you go and turn stuff in on time
